# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

args.text: Yes — for the POMDP part, the answer is: a POMDP is a partially observable Markov decision process, meaning the agent cannot directly see the full underlying state. It only gets observations, so it must keep a belief about the hidden state and sometimes take actions to gather more information. In your build, you can say the learner/agent only sees part of the environment (for example, visible files/messages), so the hidden state includes things like true attention or complete context. That’s why observation and state are not the same.
